name: Badagry Deep Sea Port
type: Greenfield deepwater container and transshipment port
summary: Largest single proposed Nigerian port project; a deepwater gateway at Badagry in Lagos State.
description: Badagry Deep Sea Port is a greenfield facility promoted by the Badagry Port Development Limited (BPDL) consortium, hosted by 12 Badagry communities. Conceived in 2012 and repeatedly re-launched, it is pitched as one of Africa's largest deepwater ports and a West African transshipment hub, with a planned free-zone component.
statusDetail: In September 2026 the Federal Government and APM Terminals (A.P. Moller-Maersk) signed a Memorandum of Understanding committing both parties to exclusive negotiations. Physical construction has not started.
mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy) and APM Terminals
mouSignificance: The MoU commits the parties to exclusive negotiations on Badagry Port. It was signed by Vincent Clerc (Group CEO, A.P. Moller-Maersk) and Didi Ndiomu (Managing Director, Badagry Port Development Limited and Quinn McGrath Marine and Environmental Services).

milestones.event: Concept conceived during the administration of Babatunde Fashola.
Governor Sanwo-Olu announces a US$2.59bn Badagry seaport and free zone, with construction targeted for June 2022.
Federal Government and APM Terminals sign MoU to develop the proposed Badagry Deep Seaport.

capacity: Positioned to handle larger container vessels and cargo for West and Central African markets.
significance: Intended West African transshipment and regional gateway.

name: Lekki Blue Sea Port
type: Proposed deepwater port at the Lekki Free Trade Zone
summary: A second, separate deepwater port proposed for the Lekki Free Trade Zone, distinct from the operational Lekki Deep Sea Port.
description: Lekki Blue Sea Port is a distinct proposal from the operating Lekki Deep Sea Port at Itoke village. In October 2023 the Federal Ministry of Works signed a construction contract MoU with China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd for the project at the Lekki Free Trade Zone, alongside wider Nigeria-China infrastructure MoUs.
statusDetail: Construction contract MoU signed in October 2023. No groundbreaking or physical works had been reported at the time of writing.
mouParties: Federal Ministry of Works and China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd
mouSignificance: Signed in Beijing at the 3rd Belt and Road Initiative Forum, witnessed by Vice President Kashim Shettima, as part of about US$2bn in Nigeria-China MoUs. The signing was led by Minister of Works Dave Umahi.

milestones.event: The separate Lekki Deep Sea Port is inaugurated by President Buhari.
Ministry of Works and China Harbour Engineering sign the Lekki Blue Sea Port MoU at the 3rd BRI Forum, Beijing.

significance: Would add deepwater capacity alongside the operating Lekki port.

name: Olokola Deep Sea Port
type: Greenfield deepwater port and export processing zone
summary: Ondo State's approved deep sea port project, originally paired with the Olokola Free Trade Zone.
description: Olokola was first conceived with an accompanying Olokola Free Trade Zone and remained stalled for roughly two decades, with the original location failing to materialise from about 2004. Efforts were renewed from 2017 and the Federal Executive Council approved the establishment of a deep sea port in Ondo State in May 2023. Ogun State separately announced plans in November 2023 to sign a private-sector MoU for an Olokola seaport in Ogun Waterside, reflecting a long-running jurisdictional claim over the site.
statusDetail: Approved by the Federal Executive Council in May 2023 after state and federal due diligence. Physical works have not started, and the site is claimed by both Ondo and Ogun State.
mouSigned: Announced 30 November 2023 (Ogun State / Organised Private Sector); not confirmed as executed
mouParties: Ogun State Government and the Organised Private Sector (stated intent)
mouSignificance: Governor Dapo Abiodun said the state would soon sign an MoU with private-sector players on the Olokola seaport, alongside the planned Kajola dry port and Gateway Agro-Cargo International Airport.

milestones.event: Original Olokola port/free-zone concept stalls.
Renewed push under Governor Akeredolu, with due diligence by state and federal government.
Federal Executive Council approves establishment of an Ondo State deep sea port.
Ogun State announces intent to sign a private-sector MoU for Olokola.

name: Ibom Deep Sea Port (Akanassa)
summary: Akwa Ibom's long-running PPP deep seaport at Akanassa in Mbo LGA; approved but repeatedly stalled.
description: The project began as the Ibaka Deep Seaport before moving to Akanassa in Mbo LGA. It is a PPP sponsored by the Federal Ministry of Transportation, the Nigerian Ports Authority and the Akwa Ibom State Government, with PricewaterhouseCoopers and GMAPS as advisers. Construction stalled after host-community opposition to a possible relocation, prompting contractor withdrawals, and has since been under revival.
statusDetail: The Outline Business Case was approved in 2015 and a phase-one tranche in December 2020, but construction has not begun. Following community opposition and contractor withdrawal, the Akwa Ibom government resumed engagement with China Harbour Engineering Company in 2022.
mouParties: Federal Government, Akwa Ibom State Government and Nigerian Ports Authority (PPP); preferred bidder Bolloré Africa Logistics / PowerChina consortium
mouSignificance: Bolloré Africa Logistics and PowerChina International were selected as preferred bidder with a 50-year operating franchise, with China Harbour Engineering Company as reserved bidder. A 50-year concession was approved in December 2016.

milestones.event: Inception planning begins; project originally named Ibaka Deep Seaport.
Federal Executive Council approves the Outline Business Case under a PPP model.
A 50-year concession period is approved for investors.
Bolloré–PowerChina consortium emerges as preferred bidder after an RFP process.
FEC approves US$2.016bn for phase one.
Renewed talks with China Harbour Engineering Company after earlier contractor withdrawal.

significance: Southeast Nigeria's flagship approved greenfield deep sea port.

name: Bakassi Deep Sea Port
type: Greenfield deepwater port and industrial park
summary: A 16 m-draft deep sea port concept for the Bakassi peninsula, bundled with a large industrial park.
description: Bakassi Deep Sea Port is a greenfield 16 m-draft port planned as the anchor of a 7,000-hectare Bakassi Industrial Park, intended to serve the North East as well as Chad and Niger Republic. Transaction advisers, including China Harbour, supported early structuring work under a project steering committee.
statusDetail: A construction agreement for preliminary works was signed with China Harbour in November 2017, following project steering committee approvals in 2016. Physical construction has not commenced.
mouParties: Cross River State Government and China Harbour Engineering Company
mouSignificance: The agreement covered preliminary works for the Bakassi Deep Seaport and was described at the time as signalling commencement of the project. It is one of the five ports the NPA later listed as having completed federal approvals and compliance steps.

milestones.event: Conceptual and technical studies completed.
Project steering committee approval received.
Project steering committee inaugurated.
Cross River State signs preliminary works construction agreement with China Harbour.

significance: Planned North East and Central African gateway via a 7,000 ha industrial park.

name: Bonny Deep Seaport
type: River-mouth deep sea port on a DBFOT concession
summary: A relocated greenfield deep sea port on Bonny Island, pitched as a 500,000 TEU facility.
description: Bonny Deep Seaport was first sited at Finima but relocated to Bonny Island after NNPC pipelines along the access channel blocked dredging at the original site. The new site has a natural draft of about 17 metres. The project is to be delivered by CCECC Nigeria Limited on a DBFOT basis and was flagged off by President Buhari in March 2022 alongside the Port Harcourt–Maiduguri rail line and a Railway Industrial Park.
status: Flagged off · awaiting full federal approval
statusDetail: Flagged off in March 2022 but reported as still lacking Federal Executive Council approval later that year. It was subsequently listed among the five approved deep seaport projects once approvals and compliance were completed.
mouSigned: Flagged off March 2022; federal approval completed later
mouParties: Federal Government and CCECC Nigeria Limited (DBFOT)
mouSignificance: The March 2022 flag-off covered roughly US$3.2bn when the seaport was bundled with the Port Harcourt–Maiduguri rail line and the Railway Industrial Park.

milestones.event: Minister of Transportation visits the Finima site to reconfirm location.
President Buhari flags off the seaport, the rail line and the Railway Industrial Park.
Site relocated from Finima to Bonny Island over NNPCL pipelines; still awaiting FEC approval.

capacity: 500,000 TEU per annum; 100,000 DWT general cargo berth; 275.22 ha.
significance: Planned eastern deepwater hub linked to the Port Harcourt–Maiduguri rail corridor.

name: Agge Deep Sea Port
summary: A US$3bn PPP deep seaport for southern Bayelsa that is active but still short of federal approval.
description: Agge Deep Sea Port in Ekeremor LGA was formally announced in 2017, when Bayelsa acquired 15,000 hectares and inaugurated a 14-member implementation committee. Public reporting stalled between 2021 and 2023, then revived after the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy was created. Bayelsa has since established a dedicated state Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy.
statusDetail: Not included in the batch of five ports the NPA reported as having completed federal approvals, because the Outline and Full Business Cases were incomplete, a transaction adviser was still being appointed, and evacuation corridors were unfinished. Concession terms were being restructured from 25 years to 40–45 years.
mouSigned: Not signed to date; federal and state MoU discussions ongoing
mouParties: Bayelsa State Government, Federal Government and a private investor (PPP)
mouSignificance: A federal steering committee visited the site to accelerate approval. A joint steering committee is expected to coordinate the financial, technical and environmental workstreams needed for federal clearance.

milestones.event: Bayelsa announces the project, acquires 15,000 ha and inaugurates an implementation committee.
Public progress stalls while background discussions continue.
Interest revived under the new Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy.
Minister of Marine and Blue Economy leads a delegation to Bayelsa to accelerate the project.

capacity: PPP scope reduced to about 7,000 ha; concession being restructured to 40–45 years.
significance: Bayelsa's flagship maritime project and a designated blue-economy asset.

name: Ogidigben Deep Sea Port
summary: An early-stage Delta State deep sea port concept reported alongside the national pipeline of planned ports.
description: Ogidigben has been named in industry reporting as one of Nigeria's proposed deep sea ports, alongside the Lagos, Ondo, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River and Rivers projects. Unlike the Badagry, Ibom, Bakassi and Bonny projects it has not appeared in federal approval announcements, and no concession, contract or construction milestone has been publicly recorded.
status: Conceptual · no recorded approval or MOU
statusDetail: Named as a proposed deep sea port in industry reporting. No federal approval, MoU, transaction adviser or concession has been publicly announced for the site.
mouSignificance: The project has not attracted a publicly announced MoU or partner, unlike the other Delta-area proposals.

milestones.event: Named in industry reporting as one of Nigeria's proposed deep sea ports.
